clue.text: Sailors in revolutionary vessel got roasted

indicators.note: the sailors are placed inside the turned-round vessel
something revolutionary turns over, so the vessel's word is read backwards

parts.note: a tub is a vessel or container
RN is the Royal Navy, the British fleet's sailors

explanation.surface: Seamen aboard a rebel ship got sunburnt.
explanation.walkthrough: 'vessel' suggests a ship given the sailors, but it is a tub, turned by 'revolutionary' to BUT before 'in' does its work; 'got' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: Food that has been roasted too long is scorched, a past-participle match.

clue.text: The girl writing two articles about mousse

indicators.note: the two articles go around the mousse, enclosing it

parts.note: AN and A are the two indefinite articles, run together
hair mousse is a styling gel

explanation.surface: A girl writes a piece involving chocolate mousse with a couple of articles.
explanation.walkthrough: 'about' puts the articles AN and A either side of GEL; 'writing' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: Angela is a girl's name, so it stands for a particular girl.

clue.text: An unusual person breaks barrier on Germany

indicators.note: something that breaks is smashed up, so the barrier's letters are reshuffled

parts.note: D is the international vehicle code for Germany

explanation.surface: Someone eccentric smashes through a border fence into Germany.
explanation.walkthrough: 'breaks' looks like a verb acting on the barrier physically, but it rearranges that word to RAREBIR; the Germany code goes after it.
explanation.definitionFit: A rare bird is an idiom for an exceptional individual seldom met.

clue.text: Material made of steel, as ticket shows

indicators.note: the word is made out of letters running across these clue words

explanation.surface: A ticket reveals what a garment's fabric is made of.
explanation.walkthrough: The letters run through 'stEEL, AS TICket'; 'shows' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: Elastic is a stretchy fabric or cord used in clothing.

clue.text: Food that's a custom on board ship

indicators.note: being on board a vessel means being inside it

parts.note: SS stands for steamship
a usage is a custom or habitual practice

explanation.surface: Some dish is a traditional practice aboard a vessel.
explanation.walkthrough: 'on board' is a stock container signal: whatever is on board a ship sits between the letters of the steamship abbreviation.
explanation.definitionFit: Sausages are a meat product eaten as a meal.

clue.text: Not partaking in test ban review

indicators.note: a review looks the words over again, signalling their letters are rearranged

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: Someone abstains from a debate about the nuclear test-ban treaty.
explanation.walkthrough: 'review' rearranges IN TEST BAN.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone abstinent refrains from indulging, especially in drink.

clue.text: Go with chart to deck

parts.note: a go is a turn in a game
a table is a chart of data

explanation.surface: Someone is told to go with a chart to punch a person.
explanation.definitionFit: A record deck is the rotating platter on which a vinyl disc plays.

clue.text: Cat, born black, was found in Scottish river

indicators.note: the two letters are found inside the river's name

parts.note: the Tay is Scotland's longest river
B is the pencil abbreviation for black

explanation.surface: A dark-coated newborn cat was found in a Scottish river.
explanation.walkthrough: 'was found in' puts B and B inside TAY.
explanation.definitionFit: A tabby is a striped domestic feline.

clue.text: Help with script

definitions.meaning: to lend a ... is to give help

explanation.definitionFit: Help: assistance, as in giving a hand; script: one's handwriting style.

clue.text: Numbers found in steering wheels

indicators.note: to wheel is to turn about, so the letters are turned into a new order

explanation.surface: Figures are displayed on modern steering wheels.
explanation.walkthrough: 'wheels' rearranges STEERING; 'found in' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: Integers are whole numbers.

clue.text: Resources placed on board a ship

indicators.note: being on board a vessel means being inside it

parts.note: SS stands for steamship
something set down has been placed

explanation.surface: Supplies are loaded onto a vessel.
explanation.walkthrough: 'on board' signals the container: the placed item goes aboard the vessel, splitting the steamship abbreviation's two letters.
explanation.definitionFit: Assets are holdings of value a firm or person can draw on.

clue.text: Transport duty has one

parts.note: a duty is a tax levied on goods
I is the Roman numeral for one

explanation.surface: A levy on transport includes one charge.
explanation.definitionFit: A cab is a form of hired road transport.

clue.text: Poor editing over news leader!

indicators.note: the letters are knocked over and set up in a new order
a leader comes first, so the first letter of news is taken

explanation.surface: A newspaper's poor editing over the front-page editorial.
explanation.walkthrough: 'over' rearranges EDITING with N, the first letter of 'news' ('leader').
explanation.definitionFit: Indigent means needy, lacking money.

clue.text: Current ruler accepted by no old ruler

indicators.note: something accepted is taken in, so it sits inside the other word

parts.note: ER, Elizabeth Regina, was the reigning queen when this was set

explanation.surface: The present monarch is welcomed by no former monarch.
explanation.walkthrough: 'accepted by' signals the container. Nero was a Roman emperor; 'Current' means reigning, not electrical.
explanation.definitionFit: Nero was an emperor of ancient Rome.

clue.text: Get singer to perform "good morning", for example

indicators.note: performing the words acts them out differently, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: Ask a vocalist to sing a breakfast-show jingle.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to perform' rearranges GET SINGER.
explanation.definitionFit: Saying good morning is one example of a salutation.

clue.text: Nation's expert on resistance

indicators.note: in an across clue one word placed on another comes after it

parts.note: R is the physics symbol for electrical resistance
an ace is an expert

explanation.surface: A country's specialist in resistance movements.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Nation's' reads as 'nation is'.
explanation.definitionFit: A race is a people or nation of common descent.

clue.text: When note was added on snakes

parts.note: as can mean when, as in 'as I left'
PS, postscript, is a note added at the end of a letter

explanation.surface: Some snakes were written about in a postscript.
explanation.walkthrough: 'on' is a link word placing the note after AS.
explanation.definitionFit: Asps are small venomous serpents.

clue.text: Estate making good sandwiches

parts.note: a round is a set of sandwiches made from two slices of bread

explanation.surface: A country house kitchen turning out fine sandwiches.
explanation.walkthrough: 'sandwiches' looks like a container signal but is just ROUNDS; 'making' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: The grounds are the land surrounding a large house.

clue.text: Inconvenient, drawn-out process

indicators.note: to process material is to work it over, so the letters are reworked

explanation.surface: A tediously lengthy procedure is a nuisance.
explanation.walkthrough: 'process' rearranges DRAWNOUT.
explanation.definitionFit: Untoward means unfavourable or awkward for the circumstances.

clue.text: Stirring, or using whisk

indicators.note: whisking beats things about, so the letters are mixed up

explanation.surface: A cook mixes the batter with a spoon or with a whisk.
explanation.walkthrough: 'whisk' rearranges OR USING.
explanation.definitionFit: Rousing means exciting or inspiring, as stirring music does.

clue.text: Worked in drama — with Edward!

parts.note: an opera is a musical drama
Ted is a short form of Edward

explanation.surface: A man named Edward got a job in theatre.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in' and 'with' are links.
explanation.definitionFit: A machine that operated was functioning or working.

clue.text: Support for new pence

parts.note: pro means in favour of
p is the abbreviation for pence after decimalisation, once called new pence

explanation.surface: A case is made for decimal coins.
explanation.definitionFit: A prop is a support that holds something up.

clue.text: Cash that is found in studies

indicators.note: the abbreviation is found inside the other word

parts.note: a student reads a subject, studies it
ie, id est, means that is

explanation.surface: Money turns up in a person's den.
explanation.walkthrough: 'found in' signals the container. 'Readies' is British slang for cash in hand.
explanation.definitionFit: Readies is slang for banknotes, ready money.

clue.text: Try and create a precedent?

parts.note: a legal trial whose verdict will set a principle for later disputes

explanation.definitionFit: A test case is a lawsuit whose ruling establishes law for later similar suits.

clue.text: Skimmed freight in old ship

indicators.note: skimming takes off the top, so the first letter is removed

parts.note: cargo is freight

explanation.surface: Ancient vessel loaded with lightly packed goods.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Skimmed' drops the C from CARGO; 'in' is a link. The Argo was Jason's ship in Greek myth.
explanation.definitionFit: The Argo was the vessel of Jason and the Argonauts in myth.

clue.text: A quarter with positive views

parts.note: E, east, is one of the four compass quarters
yes is a positive answer

explanation.surface: A district with favourable outlooks.
explanation.walkthrough: 'with' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: One's eyes are one's sight, so views or opinions, as in 'in my eyes'.

clue.text: Last finale for banker

parts.note: a finale is the end
a river has banks, so in crosswords a banker is a river; the Ure is a Yorkshire river

explanation.surface: The final bet for a gambler's sure thing.
explanation.walkthrough: 'banker' means a river, here the Ure in Yorkshire; 'for' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: To last is to persist or survive over time.

clue.text: A quaintly pleasing sort of accent

parts.note: cute means attractive in a quaint or endearing way

explanation.surface: A charmingly quirky way of speaking.
explanation.definitionFit: An acute is a diacritical mark, the rising stroke as in café.

clue.text: Large old liberal speaking to dignitary

parts.note: big means large

indicators.note: speaking means the word is heard rather than read, giving a sound-alike

parts.note: the Whigs were the forerunners of the Liberal Party

explanation.surface: A portly former Liberal MP addresses a VIP.
explanation.walkthrough: 'speaking' turns WHIG into its sound-alike WIG; 'to' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: A bigwig is an important person, a VIP.

clue.text: Hopeless plan to take a late dip

parts.note: the late means dead
to duck is to dip under water

explanation.surface: A doomed idea to go for a swim at night.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to take a' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: A dead duck is an idiom for a scheme bound to fail.

clue.text: A child's horse from within gives trouble

parts.note: gee-gee is a childish word for horse

indicators.note: only the inner letters of the word from are taken

explanation.surface: A youngster's rocking horse is causing problems.
explanation.walkthrough: 'within' takes RO from 'from'; 'gives' is a link. Aggro is British slang for aggressive trouble.
explanation.definitionFit: Aggro is slang for hostility or bother.

clue.text: Pollute river, throwing crates in

indicators.note: the shuffled letters go inside the river's name

parts.note: the Dee is a river in Wales, England and Scotland

indicators.note: throwing things scatters them, so the letters are mixed up

explanation.surface: Someone fouls a river by dumping crates into it.
explanation.walkthrough: 'throwing' rearranges the crates to SECRAT, and 'in' puts that inside the river; 'river' could be many, but the Dee fits the letters.
explanation.definitionFit: To desecrate is to defile something sacred.
